title: UP BOARD CLASS 1 — Environmental Studies | Earth Sky Stars
description: Subject-wise test on Earth Sky Stars (Environmental Studies) for UP BOARD CLASS 1. 1Q.
subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What do we see in the sky during the day?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the main celestial body visible in the sky during the day, providing light and warmth.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What do we usually see in the sky during the daytime?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the main object we see in the sky during the daytime, giving us light and warmth.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: Which of these twinkles brightly in the night sky?
questions.explanation: Stars are tiny, bright objects that appear to twinkle in the dark night sky.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What color is the sky usually on a clear, sunny day?
questions.explanation: On a clear day, the sky usually appears blue.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: Which object gives us light and warmth during the day?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the primary source of light and warmth for the Earth during the day.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: When do we usually see the Moon shining brightly in the sky?
questions.explanation: The Moon is typically visible and shines brightly in the sky at night.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: If you look up at the dark sky and see many tiny, bright, twinkling lights, what are they?
questions.explanation: The tiny, bright, twinkling lights seen scattered across the dark night sky are stars.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What makes the sky bright in the morning after it has been dark all night?
questions.explanation: The rising of the Sun in the morning brings light and makes the sky bright.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: Which of these is generally NOT seen in large numbers in the sky during the day?
questions.explanation: While the Sun, clouds, and birds are common sights during the day, many stars are typically only visible in the dark night sky.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: If it is very early morning and the Sun is just starting to appear on the horizon, what special colors might you see in the eastern sky?
questions.explanation: During sunrise (early morning), the sky often displays beautiful colors like orange, pink, and red as the sunlight passes through more of the Earth's atmosphere.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: A little fox wakes up and sees a big, bright, round object in the dark sky, and many tiny lights around it. The fox knows it's time to find its way home in the dark. What time of day is it?
questions.explanation: Seeing a big, bright, round object (Moon) and many tiny lights (stars) in a dark sky indicates it is nighttime. Foxes are often active at night.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What do we see in the sky during the day?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the main celestial body visible in the sky during the day, providing light and warmth.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: Which of these gives us light and heat naturally?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a natural source of light and heat for the Earth. Lamps, fire, and torches are man-made sources.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What do we see in the sky at night, along with the Moon?
questions.explanation: At night, when the Sun is not visible, we can see the Moon and many twinkling stars in the sky.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What is the usual color of the sky on a clear, sunny day?
questions.explanation: On a clear day, the sky appears blue due to the scattering of sunlight by the Earth's atmosphere.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: When does the Sun usually appear in the sky, marking the beginning of a new day?
questions.explanation: The Sun rises in the morning, signaling the start of the day.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: Imagine it is dark outside, and you see a bright, round object and many tiny, twinkling lights in the sky. What time of day is it?
questions.explanation: Seeing a bright, round object (the Moon) and tiny, twinkling lights (stars) in a dark sky means it is nighttime.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: Why do the stars look very small to us, even though some are very big?

options.text: They are very, very far away

questions.explanation: Stars appear small because they are at immense distances from Earth.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: What is the name of the planet where we live?
questions.explanation: We live on the planet called Earth. The Moon is Earth's natural satellite, and the Sun is a star.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: During the daytime, even though stars are always in the sky, why can't we see them?

options.text: Stars go to sleep in the day
The Sun's light is too bright

questions.explanation: The Sun's intense brightness during the day makes it impossible for us to see the much fainter light from distant stars.
questions.subject: upbo1-evs

questions.question: A child looks up at the sky and sees many dark clouds. What might they not be able to see clearly because of these clouds?
questions.explanation: Dark clouds block our view of celestial bodies like the Sun, Moon, and stars, making them difficult or impossible to see.

questions.explanation: The Sun is the primary source of light and heat for the Earth during the daytime.

questions.question: What happens when the sun sets?
questions.explanation: When the sun sets, the day ends and night begins, making the sky dark.

questions.question: If you see many tiny, twinkling lights in the sky, what time of day is it most likely?
questions.explanation: The tiny, twinkling lights are stars, which are best seen in the dark night sky after the sun has set.

questions.question: What do clouds sometimes bring to the Earth?
questions.explanation: Clouds gather in the sky and are responsible for bringing rain, which is essential for life on Earth.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the Moon?

options.text: It is seen only during the day.
It appears to change its shape.

questions.explanation: The Moon goes through different phases (like crescent, half, and full moon) over a month, making it appear to change its shape.

questions.question: Imagine you are looking out of your window. Everything is bright and you can see a large, very bright ball in the sky. What is it?
questions.explanation: The object described as a large, very bright ball that makes everything bright during the day is the Sun. The moon is visible at night and does not make everything bright.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of events from morning till night?

options.text: Stars appear -> Sun rises -> Moon appears
Moon appears -> Sun rises -> Stars appear
Sun rises -> Moon appears -> Stars appear
Sun rises -> Stars appear -> Moon appears

questions.explanation: The Sun rises in the morning. After the sun sets, the Moon may become visible, and then as it gets darker, stars appear in the night sky.
